revision.text:
{{afc comment|1=It appears an enwiki page was made around the same time I made this one at [[:en:Saminaga Shrine]]. Might be worth overwriting this one since that one seems better.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:58, 25 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Saminaga Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Saminaga-jinja 04.jpg|280px]]
{{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=270}} |location = {{ill|Shima City, Mie Prefecture|ja|志摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima City, Mie Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Isobe Town, Eribara|ja|磯部町恵利原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Town, Eribara|qq=}} 1273 |ISO = JP-24 | Latitude = 34 | Lat minute = 22 | Lat second = 30.8 | Longitude = 136 | Long minute = 48 | Long second = 12.5 |deity = {{ill|Toshigami|ja|年神|1=Toshigami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|qq=}} (Ōtoshi no Kami) |Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (small Rank)
Subordinate shrine of {{ill|Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa-no-Miya|qq=}} |consecration_year = Traditionally dated to the 27th year of Emperor Suinin |Main Hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} |Alias = Ōtoshi Shrine, Ho-otoshi-no-miya, Ho-otoshi-san |Related Sites = |Festival = |Rituals = |Label Position = left |Map = Japan Mie#Japan }} [[File:Saminaga-jinja 06.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Saminaga Shrine''' (佐美長神社) is a subordinate shrine of the {{ill|Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa-no-Miya|qq=}}, which is an auxiliary shrine of the {{ill|Inner Shrine of Ise|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inner Shrine of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}. This article also covers the {{ill|Saminaga Gomae Shrine|ja|佐美長御前神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saminaga Gomae Shrine|qq=}}, located within the same precincts and managed by Izawa-no-Miya. == Overview == Located in {{ill|Eribara, Shima City|ja|磯部町恵利原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eribara, Shima City|qq=}}, in a region called Kawabe (川辺), the shrine sits atop a hill at an elevation of about 10 meters.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：403ページ谷川 編（1986）：171ページ The current site of the shrine is said to have been either below sea level or a wetland area until the Edo period or has been revered on the hill since ancient times.式内社研究会 編（1990）：607ページ According to the "Yamato-hime-no-mikoto Seiki," it was said to be enshrined alongside Izawa-no-Miya, but the "Antei 2nd Year Naiku Sengu Record" indicates it was located to the southwest.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：400ページ The shrine is approximately 800 meters from Izawa-no-Miya.伊勢文化舎（2008）：91 - 92ページ The path connecting the two shrines is called "Gokō-michi," and it is said that the deity used to travel between the shrines.中野（1981）：18ページ The "Ise Ryōgū Bekkyū Setsumatsusha" lists the shrine as a subordinate shrine of the Inner Shrine but has been managed by Izawa-no-Miya since modern times.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：402ページ Among the five shrines under Izawa-no-Miya’s management, Saminaga Shrine holds the highest Rank.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：17ページ == Structure == The shrine hall is built in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} style, with a plank roof, railings, and steps.式内社研究会 編（1990）：610ページ Unusually for shrines under the Ise Jingu, it faces east. The shrine relocates north-south during each {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|lt=Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}} cycle, making it unique within Ise Jingu.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：410ページ The orientation may have been influenced by Izawa Bay to the east. A {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torii|qq=}} gate stands along the road, with 36 stone steps leading to the shrine.学研パブリッシング（2013）：72ページ == deity == The enshrined deity is {{ill|Toshigami|ja|年神|1=Toshigami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|qq=}}, also known as Ōtoshi no Kami.伊勢文化舎（2008）：92ページ Interpretations of the deity range from an agricultural god to a child of {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|スサノオ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}.式内社研究会 編（1990）：609ページ == Overview == It is enshrined in a region ({{ill|Region|ja|地域|lt=Region|lt_ja=地域|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Region|qq=}}) commonly known as “Kawabe” (川辺, kawabe), located at Aza Ho-ochi in {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Shima City|ja|志摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Isobe Town, Eribara|ja|磯部町恵利原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Town, Eribara|qq=}}磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：403ページ. The enshrinement site is on a hill with an elevation of approximately 10{{ill|meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/meter|qq=}}谷川 編（1986）：171ページ. The current location of {{ill|Osami Naga Shrine|ja|佐美長神社|lt=Osami Naga Shrine|lt_ja=佐美長神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osami Naga Shrine|qq=}} is subject to two theories: one posits that until the Edo period it was situated below sea level or in a {{ill|wetland|ja|湿地|lt=wetland|lt_ja=湿地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/wetland|qq=}} area and was later relocated to its present site, while the other asserts that it has been enshrined from ancient times due to its position on a slightly elevated hill式内社研究会 編（1990）：607ページ. According to the ''Wakahime no Mikoshuuki'' (倭姫命世記), it is enshrined in the same location as {{ill|Izanomiya|ja|伊雑宮|lt=Izanomiya|lt_ja=伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanomiya|qq=}}; however, the ''{{ill|Antei Era|ja|安貞|lt=Antei Era|lt_ja=安貞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Antei Era|qq=}} Ni-nen Naigu Sengenki'' (二年内宮遷宮記) records that the {{ill|Great Taiso Shrine|ja|大歳神社|lt=Great Taiso Shrine|lt_ja=大歳神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Taiso Shrine|qq=}} is worshipped with its front facing southwest (【坤（ひつじさる＝南西）】)磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：400ページ. The distance between {{ill|Izanomiya|ja|伊雑宮|lt=Izanomiya|lt_ja=伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanomiya|qq=}}, which oversees {{ill|Osami Naga Shrine|ja|佐美長神社|lt=Osami Naga Shrine|lt_ja=佐美長神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osami Naga Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Osami Naga Onmae Shrine|ja|佐美長御前神社|lt=Osami Naga Onmae Shrine|lt_ja=佐美長御前神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osami Naga Onmae Shrine|qq=}}, is approximately 800{{ill|meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/meter|qq=}}伊勢文化舎（2008）：91 - 92ページ. The road connecting Izanomiya and Osami Naga Shrine is called “Gokou-michi” (御幸道), and it is said that {{ill|Kami|ja|神 (神道)|lt=Kami|lt_ja=神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami|qq=}} once traveled between the two shrines中野（1981）：18ページ. In the ''Ise Ryōkyū Bekkyū Sessessha'' (伊勢両宮別宮摂末社), it is listed as a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂末社|lt=Subsidiary Shrine|lt_ja=末社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Subsidiary Shrine|qq=}}), but since the {{ill|Modern Period|ja|近代|lt=Modern Period|lt_ja=近代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern Period|qq=}} it has been under the jurisdiction of Izanomiya磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：402ページ. It is Ranked first among the five shrines under the jurisdiction of Izanomiya宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：17ページ. == Shrine Grounds == The {{ill|Shrine building|ja|社殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine building|qq=}} is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} style with a {{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itabuki|qq=}} roof, and it features a high balustrade and ceremonial stairs. 式内社研究会 編（1990）：610ページ The shrine building is enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamagaki|qq=}}. Unusually among the shrines under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}, it is built facing east, and with every cycle of the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|lt=Shikinen Sengu|lt_ja=式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}}, the shrine building is relocated along a north–south axis—a unique practice within Ise Grand Shrine.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：410ページ One theory for its eastern orientation is that it was intended to be oriented toward {{ill|Matoyawan|ja|的矢湾|lt=Izanora|lt_ja=伊雑ノ浦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matoyawan|qq=}}. A distributary of the Isobe River (神路川) flows through the {{ill|foothills|ja|麓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/foothills|qq=}}, within the shrine forest, and serves as the {{ill|Water source|ja|水源|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water source|qq=}} for a {{ill|Well|ja|井戸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Well|qq=}} ({{ill|Temizuya|ja|手水舎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temizuya|qq=}}) located at its base. However, the temizuya is typically fitted with a {{ill|Cover|ja|蓋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cover|qq=}}, rendering it unusable. Although the scale of the shrine grounds during the Edo period was similar to that of the present day, at that time, on the west side of the approach immediately after ascending the stone steps, there stood the subsidiary shrine “Zuiki-sha” (瑞樹社) of Osami Naga Shrine, while on the eastern side—approximately midway between the main and the old shrine sites—there was a “Kagura-den” (神楽殿), and at the very eastern end, aligned with Osami Naga Onmae Shrine, there were the subsidiary shrine “Akitsu-sha” (秋津社) and a guard station called “Yadori-jo” (宿衛所). 磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：410 - 412ページ The “Zuiki-sha” and “Akitsu-sha,” formerly subsidiary shrines of Osami Naga Shrine, were separated from the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period and were subsequently merged through {{ill|Combined Enshrinement|ja|合祀|1=co-Enshrinement|2=ja|3=合祀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Combined Enshrinement|13=User:Immanuelle/co-Enshrinement|qq=}} into the {{ill|Isobe Shrine (Komatsu City)|lt=Isobe Shrine (Komatsu City)|lt=Isobe Shrine|ja|磯部神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Shrine|qq=}}.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：414 - 412ページ ==New stuff=== == Shrine Names == {{ill|Meiji 4|ja|明治4|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji 4|qq=}} ({{ill|1871|ja|1871|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1871|qq=}}/{{ill|1872|ja|1872|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1872|qq=}}) until it was renamed "佐美長神社" (Saminaga Shrine), various shrine names such as Ootoshi-no-miya (大歳宮), Hototoshi-no-miya (穂落宮), Iiinotakamiya (飯井高宮), and Kamootanomikojinja (神織田御子神社) were used. It is believed that the names Takamiya, Iiinomiya, and Iitakamiya were proposed in the apocryphal work {{ill|Apocryphal Work|ja|偽書|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Apocryphal Work|qq=}} “{{ill|Sendaikyūjihonki Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendaikyūjihonki Taiseikyō|qq=}}”.式内社研究会 編（1990）：608ページ It is thought that by using names such as Takamiya, the status of 佐美長神社 (Saminaga Shrine) and 伊雑宮 (Izawa Shrine) was elevated, with the intention of falsely presenting 佐美長神社 as the original {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|fr|Aramatsuri_no_miya|es|Aramatsuri no miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aramatsuri-no-Miya|qq=}}.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：401ページ The first recorded occurrence of the name "佐美長神社" (Saminaga Shrine) is found in the {{ill|Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|ja|皇太神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|qq=}} of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enryaku|qq=}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/804|qq=}}), and although some documents refer to it as “佐美'''良'''神社”, in most pre‐{{ill|Early Modern period|ja|近世|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Early Modern period|qq=}} {{ill|Old Books|ja|古書|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Old Books|qq=}} before the modern era it is written as “大歳神社” or “大歳宮”.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：399 - 400ページ As a Shikinaisha, the shrine’s name was “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社” (Onajikishima Namasukamitanojinja). In “磯部町史” a hypothesis is proposed that in {{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Province|qq=}} the name was “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社”, that for the Naiku it was “佐美長神社”, and that local shrine practitioners referred to it as “大歳神社”. Even in modern times it is colloquially known as Ootoshi-sha, Hototosha, or Hototo-toshisan.伊勢文化舎（2008）：92ページ == Deity == The deity is {{ill|Year Deity|ja|年神|lt=Ootoshi-no-kami|lt_ja=大歳神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Year Deity|qq=}} (おおとしのかみ). It is said that the {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} appearing in the Hototoshi Tradition (穂落伝承) is the Year Deity. Additionally, there are theories that the “Year Deity” is a child of {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|スサノオ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, that he is either 伊佐波登美神 or his child, or that he is a god of {{ill|Grain|ja|穀物|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Grain|qq=}}.式内社研究会 編（1990）：609ページ The etymology of the name “Year Deity” is explained by one theory that “穂落 (Hototoshi)” changed into “大歳 (Ootoshi)”, and another that since cranes symbolize {{ill|Longevity|ja|長寿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Longevity|qq=}}, a great year transformed into “Year Deity”. In “宇治山田市史” the deity of 佐美長神社 is identified as “神乎多乃御子神” (Kamunotonomikojin). “神乎多乃御子神” is the deity of Onajikishima Namasukamitanojinja (identified with 佐美長神社) as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinnmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinnmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and may be regarded as the guardian deity ({{ill|Guardian Deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guardian Deity|qq=}}) of paddy fields, being the child of the god of Awajima (＝{{ill|Shima|ja|志摩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima|qq=}}). == Belief == Local residents call it “穂落としさん” (Hototoshi-san) and many pray here for a bountiful rice harvest and for protection against pests and diseases. Additionally, there is worship as a local land deity ({{ill|Land Deity|ja|地主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Land Deity|qq=}}) and observance of rituals such as ground‐breaking ceremonies ({{ill|Groundbreaking Ceremony|ja|地鎮祭|lt=Jichinsai|lt_ja=地鎮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Groundbreaking Ceremony|qq=}}) and directional protection ({{ill|Directional Deity|ja|方位神|1=Directional deity|lt=Hōi-jo|lt_ja=方位除|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directional Deity|13=User:Immanuelle/Directional deity|qq=}}). The parents of {{ill|Hayashi Gennaka|ja|林玄仲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashi Gennaka|qq=}}, an Edo‐period physician ({{ill|Childhood Name|ja|幼名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Childhood Name|qq=}}: Ōgata Hanjirō), prayed at 佐美長神社 for the blessing of children.磯部郷土史刊行会 編（1963）：263 - 264ページ Some residents consider it to be the {{ill|Toyouke Grand Shrine|ja|Toyouke Daijingu|lt=Outer Shrine|lt_ja=外宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Grand Shrine|qq=}} of Izawa Shrine. There is an oral tradition ({{ill|Oral Tradition|ja|口伝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oral Tradition|qq=}}) that states: “The sacred object ({{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体|1=Shintai|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Object|13=User:Immanuelle/Shintai|qq=}}) of 佐美長神社 is a rock ({{ill|Rock|ja|岩石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rock|qq=}}), and a substance resembling seaweed ({{ill|Seaweed|ja|藻|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seaweed|qq=}}) attached to the rock rises and falls with the tidal fluctuations ({{ill|Tide|ja|潮汐|lt=Tidal fluctuations|lt_ja=潮の干満|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tide|qq=}}), demonstrating that the deity is eternal.” The opening line of the school song ({{ill|School Song|ja|校歌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/School Song|qq=}}) of {{ill|Isobe Municipal Elementary School|ja|志摩市立磯部小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Municipal Elementary School|qq=}} is “穂落宮の丘に建つ” (“Built on the hill of Hototoshi-no-miya”), endearing the shrine to local residents.中野（1981）：16ページ == 佐美長御前神社 (Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine) == [[File:Saminaga-jinja 05.jpg|thumb|Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine (佐美長御前神社)]] 佐美長御前神社 (Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine) consists of four shrines and Ranks from second to fifth among the five shrines under the jurisdiction of Izawa Shrine. Some documents refer to it as “佐美長御前神社四社” (“The Four Shrines of Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine”). In “磯部町史” it is written as “佐美長神社御前四社”. The document “{{ill|Kambun-era Izawa Shrine Priest Conspiracy Map of Isobe Shrine|ja|寛文年間伊雑宮神主等謀計当時之磯部宮古図|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kambun-era Izawa Shrine Priest Conspiracy Map of Isobe Shrine|qq=}}” calls them the “Five Land Deity Shrines”, while “志陽略誌” records them as “月読宮・熊野遥拝社・子易ノ社”.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：404ページ Four small shrines are lined up on the left side facing south toward 佐美長神社. All four are built in the Shimmeizukuri style with wooden plank roofing. The deity here is considered to be 佐美長御前神 (Saminaga Mikenomiya), pronounced “さみながみまえのかみ”. Another theory posits that it enshrines the {{ill|Spirit|ja|霊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirit|qq=}} of a {{ill|Descendant|ja|子孫|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Descendant|qq=}} of 伊佐波登美神.(according to “神宮要綱”) Meanwhile, many old texts state that the deity is unknown. == History == Artifacts from the {{ill|Jomon period|ja|縄文時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jomon period|qq=}} to the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} have been unearthed within the shrine precincts, and earthenware ({{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthenware|qq=}}) believed to have been used as offerings—predominantly dating from the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yayoi period|qq=}} to the early Kofun period—have been discovered. === From Foundation to the Middle Ages === According to “倭姫命世記”, the foundation of 佐美長神社 (Saminaga Shrine) dates to September of the 27th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Suinin|qq=}} (垂仁天皇27th year 9月) ({{ill|Hototoshi Tradition|ja|穂落伝承|lt=Discussed later|lt_ja=後述|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hototoshi Tradition|qq=}}). Furthermore, 佐美長神社 is identified with “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社” as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinnmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinnmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. On the other hand, in Nakagawa Keiga’s “大神宮儀式解” there is no {{ill|Evidence|ja|証拠|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Evidence|qq=}} to confirm that “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社” is 佐美長神社, a claim deemed hard to believe. The {{ill|Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|ja|皇太神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|qq=}} states that the rituals of 佐美長神社 are performed in accordance with those of Izawa Shrine, suggesting that it has been an affiliated shrine of Izawa Shrine since before the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heian period|qq=}}. In the section “伊雑宮祭供奉行事” of the same document, a later addition describes “佐美長神社一處、御前四社”, confirming the existence of 佐美長御前神社. However, the founding date of 佐美長御前神社 remains unknown. ==== Hototoshi Tradition ==== The Hototoshi Tradition is a tradition concerning the founding of 佐美長神社 and is recorded in “倭姫命世記”. The contents of the tradition are as follows:中野（1981）：16 - 17ページ {{Cquote|In September of the 27th year of Emperor Suinin, while the retinue of 倭姫命 was touring {{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Province|qq=}}, they encountered a single {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} repeatedly calling. 倭姫命 remarked, “This is no ordinary occurrence,” and dispatched Ōhata-shu-no-mikoto and retainer Kirama to investigate. They then discovered a rice field in which the rice was abundantly ripened, and another {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} was seen carrying rice in its beak (some accounts state it flew in carrying the rice and then dropped it). Deeply moved, 倭姫命 declared, “Even a mute bird can cultivate a field and dedicate it to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|lt=Amaterasu|lt_ja=天照大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}},” and ordered 伊佐波登美神 to have the rice harvested, which was then dedicated to Amaterasu. The rice field where the rice was growing was named “千田” (Chida), and alongside it a shrine was established. This is Izawa Shrine, and it is 佐美長神社 that enshrined {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} as the “Year Deity.”}} {{ill|Miko Kiyonao|ja|御巫清直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko Kiyonao|qq=}} criticizes this legend as having forcefully connected the Year Deity of {{ill|Asakuma Shrine|ja|朝熊神社_(伊勢市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asakuma Shrine|qq=}} to 佐美長神社. In “磯部町史” a theory is proposed that the local {{ill|Isobe Clan|ja|磯部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Clan|qq=}} established the shrine as the god of rice cultivation.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：402 - 403ページ === Early Modern Period === In the early {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, a ritual official known as “内人” (naijin) was appointed.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：406ページ In {{ill|Kambun era|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kambun era|qq=}} 2 ({{ill|1662|ja|1662|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1662|qq=}}), the long-discontinued relocation of Izawa Shrine took place, and although the {{ill|Yamada Magistrate|ja|山田奉行|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Magistrate|qq=}}, {{ill|Yagi Munenao|ja|八木宗直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Munenao|qq=}}, and Toba Domain lord {{ill|Naitō Tadamasu (Toba Domain Lord)|ja|内藤忠政 (鳥羽藩主)|lt=Naitō Tadamasu|lt_ja=内藤忠政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naitō Tadamasu (Toba Domain Lord)|qq=}} assumed responsibility for construction, the resulting shrine building was extremely small as it was merged with other subsidiary shrines.中野（1981）：70ページ Dissatisfied, the priests of Izawa Shrine mounted a direct appeal movement aimed at “restoring the divine estates,” which eventually transformed into an extremist claim asserting that Izawa Shrine is the main shrine of the Naiku. In {{ill|Kambun era|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kambun era|qq=}} 3 ({{ill|1663|ja|1663|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1663|qq=}}), they even directly appealed to {{ill|Tokugawa Ietsuna|ja|徳川家綱|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Ietsuna|qq=}}, who was en route to visit {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Tōshō-gū|qq=}}, but this was denounced as “an outrageous, unprincipled legal action,” resulting in 54 shrine priests being expelled from both {{ill|Ise Province|ja|伊勢国|lt=Ise|lt_ja=伊勢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}} and Shima. After this “Kambun Incident”, the ritual official of 大歳神社 (Ootoshi Shrine) was no longer officially appointed by the Naiku, and instead, privately-titled priests conducted the rites. Additionally, a “神楽所” (Kagurasho) was established and kagura performers were appointed. During the Edo period, the names of 秋津神社 (Akitsu Shrine) and 瑞樹神社 (Mizuki Shrine) appear as subsidiary shrines of Ootoshi Shrine. === Modern Era and Later === In Meiji 4 (1871), with the reform of the shrine system, the positions of privately-titled priests and kagura performers were abolished.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：407ページ In their place, the priests of Izawa Shrine assumed the rites at 佐美長神社, and the Kagurasho was abolished and dismantled in August of the same year. In the same year, the official shrine name was established as “佐美長神社”. The subsidiary shrines 秋津神社 (Akitsu Shrine) and 瑞樹神社 (Mizuki Shrine) were merged into 磯部神社 (Isobe Shrine) and removed from the precincts of 佐美長神社. 佐美長神社 was rebuilt in November {{ill|1909|ja|1909|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1909|qq=}} (Meiji 42), and 佐美長御前神社 was rebuilt in January {{ill|1910|ja|1910|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1910|qq=}} (Meiji 43). Subsequently, during the {{ill|1929|ja|1929|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1929|qq=}} (Shōwa 4) {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}}, the shrine was remodeled because its disordered state – featuring a {{ill|Sunoko|ja|すのこ|lt=Sunoko|lt_ja=簀子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunoko|qq=}} high balustrade with an attached bridge, a roof thatched with rushes, and a fence – was deemed unsuitable for a unified appearance.櫻井（1991）：270ページ During the {{ill|Pacific War|ja|太平洋戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pacific War|qq=}}, children from 磯部村国民学校 (now 志摩市立磯部小学校), whose school building had been requisitioned by the {{ill|153rd Division (Imperial Japanese Army)|ja|第153師団 (日本軍)|lt=Guard Unit|lt_ja=護京部隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/153rd Division (Imperial Japanese Army)|qq=}}, sometimes held classes at 佐美長神社.磯部郷土誌刊行会 編（1963）：288ページ [[File:Hootoshimiya in dismantling.jpg|thumb|Old shrine building of 佐美長神社 dismantled after the 62nd Shikinen Sengū (December 12, 2014)]] In {{ill|1959|ja|1959|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1959|qq=}} (Shōwa 34) on {{ill|September 26|ja|9月26日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/September 26|qq=}} during the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isewan Typhoon|qq=}}, a giant tree on the shrine grounds was felled. In {{ill|1994|ja|1994|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1994|qq=}} (Heisei 6), a Shikinen Sengū was carried out.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：415ページ In {{ill|2013|ja|2013|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2013|qq=}} (Heisei 25), on the {{ill|February 1|ja|2月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/February 1|qq=}} broadcast of {{ill|Mie TV|ja|三重テレビ放送|lt=Mie TV|lt_ja=三重テレビ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie TV|qq=}}’s {{ill|Television Program|ja|番組|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Television Program|qq=}}, the show {{ill|O-Ise-san|ja|お伊勢さん (テレビ番組)|lt=O-Ise-san|lt_ja=お伊勢さん|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-Ise-san|qq=}} featured guest {{ill|Madoka Mayuzumi|ja|黛まどか|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Madoka Mayuzumi|qq=}}, who visited 佐美長神社.唐沢健治"三重テレビ制作番組「お伊勢さん」好評 10回シリーズ 全国各局で放送"2013rd year 1月31日付朝日新聞朝刊、三重版25ページ == Rituals and Shikinen Sengū == As an affiliated shrine of Izawa Shrine, the rituals—from around the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heian period|qq=}} to the Middle Ages—including the {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}} and the {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}, as well as the Shikinen Sengū, were conducted in the same manner as at Izawa Shrine, with twenty bundles of rice for the {{ill|Sacrificial Meal|ja|神饌|lt=Ritual Meal|lt_ja=御饌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacrificial Meal|qq=}} and other offerings and ritual implements provided by the {{ill|Great Shrine Official|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Shrine Official|qq=}} of Naiku.式内社研究会 編（1990）：609 - 610ページ After the Middle Ages, as the Shikinen Sengū became delayed, local Isobe residents privately undertook rebuilding the shrine structures. Following the “Kambun Incident”, 大歳神社 (Ootoshi Shrine / 佐美長神社) was rebuilt under public (Naiku direct) administration, while the four Mikenomiya shrines shifted to private rebuilding. Since the Meiji period, both 佐美長神社 and 佐美長御前神社 have had the Shinto Administrative Office and the {{ill|Jōjingū-shi Office|ja|造神宮使庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōjingū-shi Office|qq=}} responsible for the Shikinen Sengū. From the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}} through the Edo period, there was a “神楽殿” (Kaguraden) where {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} was enshrined, and 36 kagura performances were offered annually, praying for national peace and abundant harvests. == Transportation == * Approximately a 16‐minute walk (about 830 {{ill|Meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meter|qq=}}) from {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Kintetsu Shima Line|ja|近鉄志摩線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Shima Line|qq=}} {{ill|Shima Isobe Station|ja|志摩磯部駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Isobe Station|qq=}}. * Approximately a 1‐minute walk (about 100 {{ill|Meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meter|qq=}}) from the “磯部小学校前” bus stop on the {{ill|Bus|ja|路線バス|lt=Bus|lt_ja=バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bus|qq=}} of {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}}, at the bus stop ({{ill|Bus Stop|ja|バス停留所|lt=Bus Stop|lt_ja=バス停|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bus Stop|qq=}}). * From the “伊勢道路入口” {{ill|National Route 167|ja|国道167号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Route 167|qq=}} {{ill|Intersection|ja|交差点|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Intersection|qq=}}, head south via Mie Prefecture Route 61 Isobe Daiō Line for about 1 minute (approximately 300 m). There is no dedicated {{ill|Parking Lot|ja|駐車場|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Parking Lot|qq=}} for 佐美長神社, but parking is available at the nearby facility of {{ill|Toba Shisei Kōiki Rengō|ja|鳥羽志勢広域連合|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toba Shisei Kōiki Rengō|qq=}} (the former {{ill|Isobe Town|ja|磯部町 (三重県)|lt=Isobe Town|lt_ja=磯部町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Town|qq=}} Town Hall). == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * Edited by the Isobe Local History Publishing Association, ''Isobe Local History'', published by the Isobe Local History Publishing Association, May 10, Showa 38, 506p. * Edited by the Isobe Town History Compilation Committee, ''Isobe Town History, Volume 2'', Isobe Town, September 1, Heisei 9, 1340p. * Edited by the Uji Yamada City Office, ''Uji Yamada City History, Volume 1'', Uji Yamada City Office, January 20, Showa 4, 862p. * {{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=}} ''Let’s Go to Ise Jingu'', Gakken Mook Shrine Pilgrimage Selection vol.1, supervised by {{ill|Minoru Sonoda|ja|薗田稔|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minoru Sonoda|qq=}}, Gakken Marketing, July 4, 2013, 82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * {{ill|Katsuyukinoshin Sakurai|ja|櫻井勝之進|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsuyukinoshin Sakurai|qq=}} ''The Prototypes and Developments of Ise Jingu'', published by {{ill|Kokusho Kankokai|ja|国書刊行会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokusho Kankokai|qq=}}, November 30, Heisei 3, 318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * Edited by {{ill|Kenichi Tanikawa|ja|谷川健一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenichi Tanikawa|qq=}}, ''The Gods of Japan — Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 6: Ise, Shima, Iga, and Kii'', published by {{ill|Hakusuisha|ja|白水社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakusuisha|qq=}}, March 31, 1986, 492p. ISBN 4-560-02216-X * ''Jinrokawa: A Brief History of Isobe'' by Junzō Nakano, Sankōsha Sōtan Insatsu, April, Showa 56, 273p. * ''O-Ise-san 125 Shrine Pilgrimage'', a separate edition of ''Ise People'', published by {{ill|Ise Bunka-sha|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Bunka-sha|qq=}}, December 23, Heisei 20, 151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shima Province|ja|志摩国の式内社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shima Province|qq=}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of 125 Shrines of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=}} * {{ill|Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa-no-miya|qq=}} * {{ill|Hayashi Gennaka|ja|林玄仲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashi Gennaka|qq=}} '''Saminaga Shrine''' (佐美長神社) == External Links == {{Commonscat|Saminaga-jinja}} {{Osm box|n|4144263874}} * [https://web.archive.org/web/20150313063413/http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m12/1202.html 佐美長神社（さみながじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [https://web.archive.org/web/20150313104849/http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m12/1203.html 佐美長御前神社四社（さみながみまえじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [http://www.kirari1000.com/www.kirari1000.com.base_data.base_data.phpQkirari_cd=00699.html 佐美長神社と鶴の穂落とし] - [[伊勢志摩きらり千選]]（一般財団法人伊勢志摩国立公園協会） {{神道 横}} {{Good article}} {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{translated page|ja|佐美長神社|version=101820810|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Shinto_shrines_in_Mie_Prefecture]] [[Category:2014th year 竣工の日本の建築物]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Saminaga Shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shima Province]] [[Category:Buildings in Shima City]] [[Category:History of Shima City]] [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings completed in 2014]] }} [[ja:佐美長神社]] [[sn:Saminaga Shrine]] [[sn:aminaga Shrine]] [[zh:%E4%BD%90%E7%BE%8E%E9%95%B7%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[en:Saminaga Shrine]]

{{afc comment|1=It appears an enwiki page was made around the same time I made this one at [[:en:Saminaga Shrine]]. Might be worth overwriting this one since that one seems better.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:58, 25 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Saminaga Shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Saminaga-jinja 04.jpg|280px]]
{{Infobox mapframe|zoom=14|marker=religious-shinto|frame-width=270}} |location = {{ill|Shima City, Mie Prefecture|ja|志摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima City, Mie Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Isobe Town, Eribara|ja|磯部町恵利原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Town, Eribara|qq=}} 1273 |ISO = JP-24 | Latitude = 34 | Lat minute = 22 | Lat second = 30.8 | Longitude = 136 | Long minute = 48 | Long second = 12.5 |deity = {{ill|Toshigami|ja|年神|1=Toshigami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|qq=}} (Ōtoshi no Kami) |Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (small Rank)
Subordinate shrine of {{ill|Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa-no-Miya|qq=}} |consecration_year = Traditionally dated to the 27th year of Emperor Suinin |Main Hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} |Alias = Ōtoshi Shrine, Ho-otoshi-no-miya, Ho-otoshi-san |Related Sites = |Festival = |Rituals = |Label Position = left |Map = Japan Mie#Japan }} [[File:Saminaga-jinja 06.jpg|thumb|Torii gate]] '''Saminaga Shrine''' (佐美長神社) is a subordinate shrine of the {{ill|Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa-no-Miya|qq=}}, which is an auxiliary shrine of the {{ill|Inner Shrine of Ise|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inner Shrine of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|qq=}}. This article also covers the {{ill|Saminaga Gomae Shrine|ja|佐美長御前神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saminaga Gomae Shrine|qq=}}, located within the same precincts and managed by Izawa-no-Miya. == Overview == Located in {{ill|Eribara, Shima City|ja|磯部町恵利原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eribara, Shima City|qq=}}, in a region called Kawabe (川辺), the shrine sits atop a hill at an elevation of about 10 meters.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：403ページ谷川 編（1986）：171ページ The current site of the shrine is said to have been either below sea level or a wetland area until the Edo period or has been revered on the hill since ancient times.式内社研究会 編（1990）：607ページ According to the "Yamato-hime-no-mikoto Seiki," it was said to be enshrined alongside Izawa-no-Miya, but the "Antei 2nd Year Naiku Sengu Record" indicates it was located to the southwest.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：400ページ The shrine is approximately 800 meters from Izawa-no-Miya.伊勢文化舎（2008）：91 - 92ページ The path connecting the two shrines is called "Gokō-michi," and it is said that the deity used to travel between the shrines.中野（1981）：18ページ The "Ise Ryōgū Bekkyū Setsumatsusha" lists the shrine as a subordinate shrine of the Inner Shrine but has been managed by Izawa-no-Miya since modern times.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：402ページ Among the five shrines under Izawa-no-Miya’s management, Saminaga Shrine holds the highest Rank.宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：17ページ == Structure == The shrine hall is built in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} style, with a plank roof, railings, and steps.式内社研究会 編（1990）：610ページ Unusually for shrines under the Ise Jingu, it faces east. The shrine relocates north-south during each {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|lt=Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}} cycle, making it unique within Ise Jingu.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：410ページ The orientation may have been influenced by Izawa Bay to the east. A {{ill|Torii|ja|鳥居|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Torii|qq=}} gate stands along the road, with 36 stone steps leading to the shrine.学研パブリッシング（2013）：72ページ == deity == The enshrined deity is {{ill|Toshigami|ja|年神|1=Toshigami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toshigami|qq=}}, also known as Ōtoshi no Kami.伊勢文化舎（2008）：92ページ Interpretations of the deity range from an agricultural god to a child of {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|スサノオ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}.式内社研究会 編（1990）：609ページ == Overview == It is enshrined in a region ({{ill|Region|ja|地域|lt=Region|lt_ja=地域|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Region|qq=}}) commonly known as “Kawabe” (川辺, kawabe), located at Aza Ho-ochi in {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ja|三重県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Shima City|ja|志摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Isobe Town, Eribara|ja|磯部町恵利原|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Town, Eribara|qq=}}磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：403ページ. The enshrinement site is on a hill with an elevation of approximately 10{{ill|meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/meter|qq=}}谷川 編（1986）：171ページ. The current location of {{ill|Osami Naga Shrine|ja|佐美長神社|lt=Osami Naga Shrine|lt_ja=佐美長神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osami Naga Shrine|qq=}} is subject to two theories: one posits that until the Edo period it was situated below sea level or in a {{ill|wetland|ja|湿地|lt=wetland|lt_ja=湿地|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/wetland|qq=}} area and was later relocated to its present site, while the other asserts that it has been enshrined from ancient times due to its position on a slightly elevated hill式内社研究会 編（1990）：607ページ. According to the ''Wakahime no Mikoshuuki'' (倭姫命世記), it is enshrined in the same location as {{ill|Izanomiya|ja|伊雑宮|lt=Izanomiya|lt_ja=伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanomiya|qq=}}; however, the ''{{ill|Antei Era|ja|安貞|lt=Antei Era|lt_ja=安貞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Antei Era|qq=}} Ni-nen Naigu Sengenki'' (二年内宮遷宮記) records that the {{ill|Great Taiso Shrine|ja|大歳神社|lt=Great Taiso Shrine|lt_ja=大歳神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Taiso Shrine|qq=}} is worshipped with its front facing southwest (【坤（ひつじさる＝南西）】)磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：400ページ. The distance between {{ill|Izanomiya|ja|伊雑宮|lt=Izanomiya|lt_ja=伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanomiya|qq=}}, which oversees {{ill|Osami Naga Shrine|ja|佐美長神社|lt=Osami Naga Shrine|lt_ja=佐美長神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osami Naga Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Osami Naga Onmae Shrine|ja|佐美長御前神社|lt=Osami Naga Onmae Shrine|lt_ja=佐美長御前神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Osami Naga Onmae Shrine|qq=}}, is approximately 800{{ill|meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/meter|qq=}}伊勢文化舎（2008）：91 - 92ページ. The road connecting Izanomiya and Osami Naga Shrine is called “Gokou-michi” (御幸道), and it is said that {{ill|Kami|ja|神 (神道)|lt=Kami|lt_ja=神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kami|qq=}} once traveled between the two shrines中野（1981）：18ページ. In the ''Ise Ryōkyū Bekkyū Sessessha'' (伊勢両宮別宮摂末社), it is listed as a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine ({{ill|Subsidiary Shrine|ja|摂末社|lt=Subsidiary Shrine|lt_ja=末社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Subsidiary Shrine|qq=}}), but since the {{ill|Modern Period|ja|近代|lt=Modern Period|lt_ja=近代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern Period|qq=}} it has been under the jurisdiction of Izanomiya磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：402ページ. It is Ranked first among the five shrines under the jurisdiction of Izanomiya宇治山田市役所 編（1929）：17ページ. == Shrine Grounds == The {{ill|Shrine building|ja|社殿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shrine building|qq=}} is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} style with a {{ill|Itabuki|ja|板葺|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itabuki|qq=}} roof, and it features a high balustrade and ceremonial stairs. 式内社研究会 編（1990）：610ページ The shrine building is enclosed by a {{ill|Tamagaki|ja|玉垣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamagaki|qq=}}. Unusually among the shrines under the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}}, it is built facing east, and with every cycle of the {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|lt=Shikinen Sengu|lt_ja=式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}}, the shrine building is relocated along a north–south axis—a unique practice within Ise Grand Shrine.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：410ページ One theory for its eastern orientation is that it was intended to be oriented toward {{ill|Matoyawan|ja|的矢湾|lt=Izanora|lt_ja=伊雑ノ浦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matoyawan|qq=}}. A distributary of the Isobe River (神路川) flows through the {{ill|foothills|ja|麓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/foothills|qq=}}, within the shrine forest, and serves as the {{ill|Water source|ja|水源|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water source|qq=}} for a {{ill|Well|ja|井戸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Well|qq=}} ({{ill|Temizuya|ja|手水舎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temizuya|qq=}}) located at its base. However, the temizuya is typically fitted with a {{ill|Cover|ja|蓋|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cover|qq=}}, rendering it unusable. Although the scale of the shrine grounds during the Edo period was similar to that of the present day, at that time, on the west side of the approach immediately after ascending the stone steps, there stood the subsidiary shrine “Zuiki-sha” (瑞樹社) of Osami Naga Shrine, while on the eastern side—approximately midway between the main and the old shrine sites—there was a “Kagura-den” (神楽殿), and at the very eastern end, aligned with Osami Naga Onmae Shrine, there were the subsidiary shrine “Akitsu-sha” (秋津社) and a guard station called “Yadori-jo” (宿衛所). 磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：410 - 412ページ The “Zuiki-sha” and “Akitsu-sha,” formerly subsidiary shrines of Osami Naga Shrine, were separated from the jurisdiction of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Grand Shrine|qq=}} during the Meiji period and were subsequently merged through {{ill|Combined Enshrinement|ja|合祀|1=co-Enshrinement|2=ja|3=合祀|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Combined Enshrinement|13=User:Immanuelle/co-Enshrinement|qq=}} into the {{ill|Isobe Shrine (Komatsu City)|lt=Isobe Shrine (Komatsu City)|lt=Isobe Shrine|ja|磯部神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Shrine|qq=}}.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：414 - 412ページ ==New stuff=== == Shrine Names == {{ill|Meiji 4|ja|明治4|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji 4|qq=}} ({{ill|1871|ja|1871|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1871|qq=}}/{{ill|1872|ja|1872|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1872|qq=}}) until it was renamed "佐美長神社" (Saminaga Shrine), various shrine names such as Ootoshi-no-miya (大歳宮), Hototoshi-no-miya (穂落宮), Iiinotakamiya (飯井高宮), and Kamootanomikojinja (神織田御子神社) were used. It is believed that the names Takamiya, Iiinomiya, and Iitakamiya were proposed in the apocryphal work {{ill|Apocryphal Work|ja|偽書|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Apocryphal Work|qq=}} “{{ill|Sendaikyūjihonki Taiseikyō|ja|先代旧事本紀大成経|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sendaikyūjihonki Taiseikyō|qq=}}”.式内社研究会 編（1990）：608ページ It is thought that by using names such as Takamiya, the status of 佐美長神社 (Saminaga Shrine) and 伊雑宮 (Izawa Shrine) was elevated, with the intention of falsely presenting 佐美長神社 as the original {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|ja|荒祭宮|fr|Aramatsuri_no_miya|es|Aramatsuri no miya|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aramatsuri-no-Miya|qq=}}.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：401ページ The first recorded occurrence of the name "佐美長神社" (Saminaga Shrine) is found in the {{ill|Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|ja|皇太神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|qq=}} of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enryaku|qq=}} 23 ({{ill|804|ja|804|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/804|qq=}}), and although some documents refer to it as “佐美'''良'''神社”, in most pre‐{{ill|Early Modern period|ja|近世|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Early Modern period|qq=}} {{ill|Old Books|ja|古書|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Old Books|qq=}} before the modern era it is written as “大歳神社” or “大歳宮”.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：399 - 400ページ As a Shikinaisha, the shrine’s name was “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社” (Onajikishima Namasukamitanojinja). In “磯部町史” a hypothesis is proposed that in {{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Province|qq=}} the name was “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社”, that for the Naiku it was “佐美長神社”, and that local shrine practitioners referred to it as “大歳神社”. Even in modern times it is colloquially known as Ootoshi-sha, Hototosha, or Hototo-toshisan.伊勢文化舎（2008）：92ページ == Deity == The deity is {{ill|Year Deity|ja|年神|lt=Ootoshi-no-kami|lt_ja=大歳神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Year Deity|qq=}} (おおとしのかみ). It is said that the {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} appearing in the Hototoshi Tradition (穂落伝承) is the Year Deity. Additionally, there are theories that the “Year Deity” is a child of {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|スサノオ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, that he is either 伊佐波登美神 or his child, or that he is a god of {{ill|Grain|ja|穀物|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Grain|qq=}}.式内社研究会 編（1990）：609ページ The etymology of the name “Year Deity” is explained by one theory that “穂落 (Hototoshi)” changed into “大歳 (Ootoshi)”, and another that since cranes symbolize {{ill|Longevity|ja|長寿|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Longevity|qq=}}, a great year transformed into “Year Deity”. In “宇治山田市史” the deity of 佐美長神社 is identified as “神乎多乃御子神” (Kamunotonomikojin). “神乎多乃御子神” is the deity of Onajikishima Namasukamitanojinja (identified with 佐美長神社) as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinnmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinnmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, and may be regarded as the guardian deity ({{ill|Guardian Deity|ja|守護神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Guardian Deity|qq=}}) of paddy fields, being the child of the god of Awajima (＝{{ill|Shima|ja|志摩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima|qq=}}). == Belief == Local residents call it “穂落としさん” (Hototoshi-san) and many pray here for a bountiful rice harvest and for protection against pests and diseases. Additionally, there is worship as a local land deity ({{ill|Land Deity|ja|地主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Land Deity|qq=}}) and observance of rituals such as ground‐breaking ceremonies ({{ill|Groundbreaking Ceremony|ja|地鎮祭|lt=Jichinsai|lt_ja=地鎮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Groundbreaking Ceremony|qq=}}) and directional protection ({{ill|Directional Deity|ja|方位神|1=Directional deity|lt=Hōi-jo|lt_ja=方位除|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Directional Deity|13=User:Immanuelle/Directional deity|qq=}}). The parents of {{ill|Hayashi Gennaka|ja|林玄仲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashi Gennaka|qq=}}, an Edo‐period physician ({{ill|Childhood Name|ja|幼名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Childhood Name|qq=}}: Ōgata Hanjirō), prayed at 佐美長神社 for the blessing of children.磯部郷土史刊行会 編（1963）：263 - 264ページ Some residents consider it to be the {{ill|Toyouke Grand Shrine|ja|Toyouke Daijingu|lt=Outer Shrine|lt_ja=外宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke Grand Shrine|qq=}} of Izawa Shrine. There is an oral tradition ({{ill|Oral Tradition|ja|口伝|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oral Tradition|qq=}}) that states: “The sacred object ({{ill|Sacred Object|ja|神体|1=Shintai|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Object|13=User:Immanuelle/Shintai|qq=}}) of 佐美長神社 is a rock ({{ill|Rock|ja|岩石|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rock|qq=}}), and a substance resembling seaweed ({{ill|Seaweed|ja|藻|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seaweed|qq=}}) attached to the rock rises and falls with the tidal fluctuations ({{ill|Tide|ja|潮汐|lt=Tidal fluctuations|lt_ja=潮の干満|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tide|qq=}}), demonstrating that the deity is eternal.” The opening line of the school song ({{ill|School Song|ja|校歌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/School Song|qq=}}) of {{ill|Isobe Municipal Elementary School|ja|志摩市立磯部小学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Municipal Elementary School|qq=}} is “穂落宮の丘に建つ” (“Built on the hill of Hototoshi-no-miya”), endearing the shrine to local residents.中野（1981）：16ページ == 佐美長御前神社 (Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine) == [[File:Saminaga-jinja 05.jpg|thumb|Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine (佐美長御前神社)]] 佐美長御前神社 (Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine) consists of four shrines and Ranks from second to fifth among the five shrines under the jurisdiction of Izawa Shrine. Some documents refer to it as “佐美長御前神社四社” (“The Four Shrines of Saminaga Mikenomiya Shrine”). In “磯部町史” it is written as “佐美長神社御前四社”. The document “{{ill|Kambun-era Izawa Shrine Priest Conspiracy Map of Isobe Shrine|ja|寛文年間伊雑宮神主等謀計当時之磯部宮古図|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kambun-era Izawa Shrine Priest Conspiracy Map of Isobe Shrine|qq=}}” calls them the “Five Land Deity Shrines”, while “志陽略誌” records them as “月読宮・熊野遥拝社・子易ノ社”.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：404ページ Four small shrines are lined up on the left side facing south toward 佐美長神社. All four are built in the Shimmeizukuri style with wooden plank roofing. The deity here is considered to be 佐美長御前神 (Saminaga Mikenomiya), pronounced “さみながみまえのかみ”. Another theory posits that it enshrines the {{ill|Spirit|ja|霊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Spirit|qq=}} of a {{ill|Descendant|ja|子孫|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Descendant|qq=}} of 伊佐波登美神.(according to “神宮要綱”) Meanwhile, many old texts state that the deity is unknown. == History == Artifacts from the {{ill|Jomon period|ja|縄文時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jomon period|qq=}} to the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} have been unearthed within the shrine precincts, and earthenware ({{ill|Earthenware|ja|土器|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Earthenware|qq=}}) believed to have been used as offerings—predominantly dating from the late {{ill|Yayoi period|ja|弥生時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yayoi period|qq=}} to the early Kofun period—have been discovered. === From Foundation to the Middle Ages === According to “倭姫命世記”, the foundation of 佐美長神社 (Saminaga Shrine) dates to September of the 27th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Suinin|qq=}} (垂仁天皇27th year 9月) ({{ill|Hototoshi Tradition|ja|穂落伝承|lt=Discussed later|lt_ja=後述|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hototoshi Tradition|qq=}}). Furthermore, 佐美長神社 is identified with “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社” as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinnmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinnmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. On the other hand, in Nakagawa Keiga’s “大神宮儀式解” there is no {{ill|Evidence|ja|証拠|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Evidence|qq=}} to confirm that “同島坐神乎多乃御子神社” is 佐美長神社, a claim deemed hard to believe. The {{ill|Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|ja|皇太神宮儀式帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōta Jingū Gishikichō|qq=}} states that the rituals of 佐美長神社 are performed in accordance with those of Izawa Shrine, suggesting that it has been an affiliated shrine of Izawa Shrine since before the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heian period|qq=}}. In the section “伊雑宮祭供奉行事” of the same document, a later addition describes “佐美長神社一處、御前四社”, confirming the existence of 佐美長御前神社. However, the founding date of 佐美長御前神社 remains unknown. ==== Hototoshi Tradition ==== The Hototoshi Tradition is a tradition concerning the founding of 佐美長神社 and is recorded in “倭姫命世記”. The contents of the tradition are as follows:中野（1981）：16 - 17ページ {{Cquote|In September of the 27th year of Emperor Suinin, while the retinue of 倭姫命 was touring {{ill|Shima Province|ja|志摩国|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Province|qq=}}, they encountered a single {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} repeatedly calling. 倭姫命 remarked, “This is no ordinary occurrence,” and dispatched Ōhata-shu-no-mikoto and retainer Kirama to investigate. They then discovered a rice field in which the rice was abundantly ripened, and another {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} was seen carrying rice in its beak (some accounts state it flew in carrying the rice and then dropped it). Deeply moved, 倭姫命 declared, “Even a mute bird can cultivate a field and dedicate it to {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|lt=Amaterasu|lt_ja=天照大神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}},” and ordered 伊佐波登美神 to have the rice harvested, which was then dedicated to Amaterasu. The rice field where the rice was growing was named “千田” (Chida), and alongside it a shrine was established. This is Izawa Shrine, and it is 佐美長神社 that enshrined {{ill|Manazuru|ja|マナヅル|lt=Manazuru|lt_ja=真名鶴|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Manazuru|qq=}} as the “Year Deity.”}} {{ill|Miko Kiyonao|ja|御巫清直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko Kiyonao|qq=}} criticizes this legend as having forcefully connected the Year Deity of {{ill|Asakuma Shrine|ja|朝熊神社_(伊勢市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asakuma Shrine|qq=}} to 佐美長神社. In “磯部町史” a theory is proposed that the local {{ill|Isobe Clan|ja|磯部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Clan|qq=}} established the shrine as the god of rice cultivation.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：402 - 403ページ === Early Modern Period === In the early {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, a ritual official known as “内人” (naijin) was appointed.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：406ページ In {{ill|Kambun era|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kambun era|qq=}} 2 ({{ill|1662|ja|1662|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1662|qq=}}), the long-discontinued relocation of Izawa Shrine took place, and although the {{ill|Yamada Magistrate|ja|山田奉行|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamada Magistrate|qq=}}, {{ill|Yagi Munenao|ja|八木宗直|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yagi Munenao|qq=}}, and Toba Domain lord {{ill|Naitō Tadamasu (Toba Domain Lord)|ja|内藤忠政 (鳥羽藩主)|lt=Naitō Tadamasu|lt_ja=内藤忠政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naitō Tadamasu (Toba Domain Lord)|qq=}} assumed responsibility for construction, the resulting shrine building was extremely small as it was merged with other subsidiary shrines.中野（1981）：70ページ Dissatisfied, the priests of Izawa Shrine mounted a direct appeal movement aimed at “restoring the divine estates,” which eventually transformed into an extremist claim asserting that Izawa Shrine is the main shrine of the Naiku. In {{ill|Kambun era|ja|寛文|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kambun era|qq=}} 3 ({{ill|1663|ja|1663|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1663|qq=}}), they even directly appealed to {{ill|Tokugawa Ietsuna|ja|徳川家綱|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Ietsuna|qq=}}, who was en route to visit {{ill|Nikkō Tōshō-gū|ja|日光東照宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nikkō Tōshō-gū|qq=}}, but this was denounced as “an outrageous, unprincipled legal action,” resulting in 54 shrine priests being expelled from both {{ill|Ise Province|ja|伊勢国|lt=Ise|lt_ja=伊勢|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}} and Shima. After this “Kambun Incident”, the ritual official of 大歳神社 (Ootoshi Shrine) was no longer officially appointed by the Naiku, and instead, privately-titled priests conducted the rites. Additionally, a “神楽所” (Kagurasho) was established and kagura performers were appointed. During the Edo period, the names of 秋津神社 (Akitsu Shrine) and 瑞樹神社 (Mizuki Shrine) appear as subsidiary shrines of Ootoshi Shrine. === Modern Era and Later === In Meiji 4 (1871), with the reform of the shrine system, the positions of privately-titled priests and kagura performers were abolished.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：407ページ In their place, the priests of Izawa Shrine assumed the rites at 佐美長神社, and the Kagurasho was abolished and dismantled in August of the same year. In the same year, the official shrine name was established as “佐美長神社”. The subsidiary shrines 秋津神社 (Akitsu Shrine) and 瑞樹神社 (Mizuki Shrine) were merged into 磯部神社 (Isobe Shrine) and removed from the precincts of 佐美長神社. 佐美長神社 was rebuilt in November {{ill|1909|ja|1909|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1909|qq=}} (Meiji 42), and 佐美長御前神社 was rebuilt in January {{ill|1910|ja|1910|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1910|qq=}} (Meiji 43). Subsequently, during the {{ill|1929|ja|1929|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1929|qq=}} (Shōwa 4) {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|神宮式年遷宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jingū Shikinen Sengū|qq=}}, the shrine was remodeled because its disordered state – featuring a {{ill|Sunoko|ja|すのこ|lt=Sunoko|lt_ja=簀子|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sunoko|qq=}} high balustrade with an attached bridge, a roof thatched with rushes, and a fence – was deemed unsuitable for a unified appearance.櫻井（1991）：270ページ During the {{ill|Pacific War|ja|太平洋戦争|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Pacific War|qq=}}, children from 磯部村国民学校 (now 志摩市立磯部小学校), whose school building had been requisitioned by the {{ill|153rd Division (Imperial Japanese Army)|ja|第153師団 (日本軍)|lt=Guard Unit|lt_ja=護京部隊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/153rd Division (Imperial Japanese Army)|qq=}}, sometimes held classes at 佐美長神社.磯部郷土誌刊行会 編（1963）：288ページ [[File:Hootoshimiya in dismantling.jpg|thumb|Old shrine building of 佐美長神社 dismantled after the 62nd Shikinen Sengū (December 12, 2014)]] In {{ill|1959|ja|1959|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1959|qq=}} (Shōwa 34) on {{ill|September 26|ja|9月26日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/September 26|qq=}} during the {{ill|Isewan Typhoon|ja|伊勢湾台風|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isewan Typhoon|qq=}}, a giant tree on the shrine grounds was felled. In {{ill|1994|ja|1994|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1994|qq=}} (Heisei 6), a Shikinen Sengū was carried out.磯部町史編纂委員会 編（1997）：415ページ In {{ill|2013|ja|2013|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/2013|qq=}} (Heisei 25), on the {{ill|February 1|ja|2月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/February 1|qq=}} broadcast of {{ill|Mie TV|ja|三重テレビ放送|lt=Mie TV|lt_ja=三重テレビ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie TV|qq=}}’s {{ill|Television Program|ja|番組|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Television Program|qq=}}, the show {{ill|O-Ise-san|ja|お伊勢さん (テレビ番組)|lt=O-Ise-san|lt_ja=お伊勢さん|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-Ise-san|qq=}} featured guest {{ill|Madoka Mayuzumi|ja|黛まどか|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Madoka Mayuzumi|qq=}}, who visited 佐美長神社.唐沢健治"三重テレビ制作番組「お伊勢さん」好評 10回シリーズ 全国各局で放送"2013rd year 1月31日付朝日新聞朝刊、三重版25ページ == Rituals and Shikinen Sengū == As an affiliated shrine of Izawa Shrine, the rituals—from around the {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heian period|qq=}} to the Middle Ages—including the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai Festival|lt=Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kannamesai|qq=}} and the {{ill|Monthly Festival|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}, as well as the Shikinen Sengū, were conducted in the same manner as at Izawa Shrine, with twenty bundles of rice for the {{ill|Sacrificial Meal|ja|神饌|lt=Ritual Meal|lt_ja=御饌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacrificial Meal|qq=}} and other offerings and ritual implements provided by the {{ill|Great Shrine Official|ja|大宮司|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Shrine Official|qq=}} of Naiku.式内社研究会 編（1990）：609 - 610ページ After the Middle Ages, as the Shikinen Sengū became delayed, local Isobe residents privately undertook rebuilding the shrine structures. Following the “Kambun Incident”, 大歳神社 (Ootoshi Shrine / 佐美長神社) was rebuilt under public (Naiku direct) administration, while the four Mikenomiya shrines shifted to private rebuilding. Since the Meiji period, both 佐美長神社 and 佐美長御前神社 have had the Shinto Administrative Office and the {{ill|Jōjingū-shi Office|ja|造神宮使庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōjingū-shi Office|qq=}} responsible for the Shikinen Sengū. From the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromachi period|qq=}} through the Edo period, there was a “神楽殿” (Kaguraden) where {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|ja|猿田彦大神|lt=Sarutahiko|lt_ja=猿田彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}} was enshrined, and 36 kagura performances were offered annually, praying for national peace and abundant harvests. == Transportation == * Approximately a 16‐minute walk (about 830 {{ill|Meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meter|qq=}}) from {{ill|Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu|qq=}} {{ill|Kintetsu Shima Line|ja|近鉄志摩線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kintetsu Shima Line|qq=}} {{ill|Shima Isobe Station|ja|志摩磯部駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shima Isobe Station|qq=}}. * Approximately a 1‐minute walk (about 100 {{ill|Meter|ja|メートル|lt=m|lt_ja=m|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meter|qq=}}) from the “磯部小学校前” bus stop on the {{ill|Bus|ja|路線バス|lt=Bus|lt_ja=バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bus|qq=}} of {{ill|Mie Kōtsū|ja|三重交通|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Kōtsū|qq=}}, at the bus stop ({{ill|Bus Stop|ja|バス停留所|lt=Bus Stop|lt_ja=バス停|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bus Stop|qq=}}). * From the “伊勢道路入口” {{ill|National Route 167|ja|国道167号|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Route 167|qq=}} {{ill|Intersection|ja|交差点|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Intersection|qq=}}, head south via Mie Prefecture Route 61 Isobe Daiō Line for about 1 minute (approximately 300 m). There is no dedicated {{ill|Parking Lot|ja|駐車場|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Parking Lot|qq=}} for 佐美長神社, but parking is available at the nearby facility of {{ill|Toba Shisei Kōiki Rengō|ja|鳥羽志勢広域連合|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toba Shisei Kōiki Rengō|qq=}} (the former {{ill|Isobe Town|ja|磯部町 (三重県)|lt=Isobe Town|lt_ja=磯部町|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isobe Town|qq=}} Town Hall). == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Bibliography == * Edited by the Isobe Local History Publishing Association, ''Isobe Local History'', published by the Isobe Local History Publishing Association, May 10, Showa 38, 506p. * Edited by the Isobe Town History Compilation Committee, ''Isobe Town History, Volume 2'', Isobe Town, September 1, Heisei 9, 1340p. * Edited by the Uji Yamada City Office, ''Uji Yamada City History, Volume 1'', Uji Yamada City Office, January 20, Showa 4, 862p. * {{ill|Gakken Publishing|ja|学研パブリッシング|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gakken Publishing|qq=}} ''Let’s Go to Ise Jingu'', Gakken Mook Shrine Pilgrimage Selection vol.1, supervised by {{ill|Minoru Sonoda|ja|薗田稔|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Minoru Sonoda|qq=}}, Gakken Marketing, July 4, 2013, 82p. ISBN 978-4-05-610047-1 * {{ill|Katsuyukinoshin Sakurai|ja|櫻井勝之進|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsuyukinoshin Sakurai|qq=}} ''The Prototypes and Developments of Ise Jingu'', published by {{ill|Kokusho Kankokai|ja|国書刊行会|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokusho Kankokai|qq=}}, November 30, Heisei 3, 318p. ISBN 4-336-03296-3 * Edited by {{ill|Kenichi Tanikawa|ja|谷川健一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenichi Tanikawa|qq=}}, ''The Gods of Japan — Shrines and Sacred Sites, Volume 6: Ise, Shima, Iga, and Kii'', published by {{ill|Hakusuisha|ja|白水社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakusuisha|qq=}}, March 31, 1986, 492p. ISBN 4-560-02216-X * ''Jinrokawa: A Brief History of Isobe'' by Junzō Nakano, Sankōsha Sōtan Insatsu, April, Showa 56, 273p. * ''O-Ise-san 125 Shrine Pilgrimage'', a separate edition of ''Ise People'', published by {{ill|Ise Bunka-sha|ja|伊勢文化舎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Bunka-sha|qq=}}, December 23, Heisei 20, 151p. ISBN 978-4-900759-37-4 == See Also == * {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shima Province|ja|志摩国の式内社一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shima Province|qq=}} * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧|lt=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|3=伊勢国の式内社一覧|1=List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of 125 Shrines of Ise|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Ise Province|qq=}} * {{ill|Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-miya|lt=Izawa-no-Miya|ja|伊雑宮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa-no-miya|qq=}} * {{ill|Hayashi Gennaka|ja|林玄仲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayashi Gennaka|qq=}} '''Saminaga Shrine''' (佐美長神社) == External Links == {{Commonscat|Saminaga-jinja}} {{Osm box|n|4144263874}} * [https://web.archive.org/web/20150313063413/http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m12/1202.html 佐美長神社（さみながじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [https://web.archive.org/web/20150313104849/http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m12/1203.html 佐美長御前神社四社（さみながみまえじんじゃ）] - 財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [http://www.kirari1000.com/www.kirari1000.com.base_data.base_data.phpQkirari_cd=00699.html 佐美長神社と鶴の穂落とし] - [[伊勢志摩きらり千選]]（一般財団法人伊勢志摩国立公園協会） {{神道 横}} {{Good article}} {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{translated page|ja|佐美長神社|version=101820810|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:Shinto_shrines_in_Mie_Prefecture]] [[Category:2014th year 竣工の日本の建築物]] [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Saminaga Shrine]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Shima Province]] [[Category:Buildings in Shima City]] [[Category:History of Shima City]] [[Category:Shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings completed in 2014]] }} [[ja:佐美長神社]] [[sn:Saminaga Shrine]] [[sn:aminaga Shrine]] [[zh:%E4%BD%90%E7%BE%8E%E9%95%B7%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] [[en:Saminaga Shrine]]
